newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines buries Marcos predecessor Macapagal.
newsitem.headline: Philippines buries Marcos predecessor Macapagal.

text.p: Former Philippine president Diosdado Macapagal, the man Ferdinand Marcos beat in an election in 1965 to start his harsh 21-year rule, was buried with state honours on Sunday at Manila's Heroes Cemetery.
An honour guard fired a 21-gun salute and an army helicopter showered the funeral with flowers in honour of Macapagal, a laundress' son who rose from poverty to become the nation's ninth president.
Macapagal died on Monday at the age of 86. He had suffered from heart and kidney problems and pneumonia.
He was president from 1961 to 1965 but lost his re-election bid to Marcos, who later declared martial law and ruled with an iron fist until he was ousted in a 1986 popular revolt.

Cardinal Jaime Sin, this Catholic nation's most influential church official, eulogised Macapagal by saying he "lost to a man who became the longest-staying dictator" of the country, a reference to Marcos.
But Macapagal has won an honor that still eludes Marcos: burial at the Heroes Cemetery, which is reserved for the nation's presidents and soldiers.
The body of Marcos, who died in exile in Hawaii in 1989, lies in state in a refrigerated mausoleum in his home province of Ilocos Norte.
Moves by his wife, former first lady Imelda Marcos, to have him laid to rest in the cemetery have been blocked by the government, which accuses the Marcoses of plundering the economy while in power.
"I am glad that they do not have to grieve for so long as I have for the last eight years for my unburied husband," Imelda Marcos said in a statement.
